Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 80, verses 11–16 (part 1 of 2):

"Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may take heed of it. It is in scriptures held in honor, exalted, purified, in the hands of scribes, noble and righteous." (80:11–16)

So this call is, in every respect, a call worthy of esteem. Its scriptures are honored, lofty and pure, and their keeping and their conveyance in the higher realm have been entrusted to hands that are righteous and noble. Therefore, whoever is associated with the Islamic call, near or far, is honored and righteous, and this call has no need for people who turn away from it and show indifference. It is meant only for those who acknowledge its loftiness and its purity, and who wish to acquire purity through it.

This is the criterion, the standard set by Allah. By it we must weigh the deeds and the intentions of others and of ourselves. This is the command of Allah, the word of Allah, and before it no word carries any weight; every act and every judgment is inferior to it.

Where was this command given, and where did this event occur? In Makkah, when the Islamic call was being pursued from every side, and the Muslims were very few in number. The Prophet ﷺ was not turning toward those influential people for any personal purpose, nor was his disregard of that blind man born of any personal motive. The sole concern before the Messenger ﷺ was the interest of the Islamic call, yet the scale of this call was different. Its values were different. It was to establish standards for people and to create traditions. This call could be successful, dignified and strong only if it set down such measures.

This was not merely an individual incident; it was a great principle. It was not a matter of ordinary moral conduct; rather, a fundamental and constitutional question was at hand: from where should people derive the standards of good and evil? From the customs of the earth or from heavenly guidance; from earthly and popular perspectives or from the presence of the Lord of Majesty, from where this principle has been laid down.

"Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the one most righteous among you" (49:13).

In this call and this movement, only that is significant which is significant in the sight of Allah, even if, in worldly terms, one is deprived of the factors that carry weight with people, such as lineage, numerical and financial strength, and other considerations that the world regards as important. If these things are devoid of faith and do not bear the colour of taqwa, they have no weight in this call. From the perspective of this movement, the important and foremost matter is that a person sets his circumstances right according to faith and taqwa.

Through this particular and individual incident, Allah intended to impress upon the minds of people this great truth and this great principle, in keeping with the Qur'anic method of reform and training, in which a great principle is drawn from an individual event and fixed in people's minds. This principle then becomes a constitutional rule.

The personality of Muhammad ﷺ was deeply affected by these instructions and by this reproof. He accepted these instructions with great zeal, and by acting upon them he put this principle and constitution into effect in the Islamic society. The structure of this new community was founded upon this principle, for it was the first brick of the Islamic society.

His first duty was determined to be that he himself should narrate this incident as a part of a Surah of the Qur'an. This was a momentous matter; only a Messenger of Allah could do it. From whatever aspect we consider it, a human being conceals his weaknesses. It was the Messenger of Allah alone who openly announced this divine reproof, and announced it in this unique manner. If there had been any leader other than a prophet, he would have become aware of his mistake and would have been more cautious in future, but the station of a prophet of Allah is of another kind. The horizons of the prophethood are of another kind, very lofty and far-reaching.

It was the Prophet alone who, in the most difficult and delicate circumstances, announced this principle before the influential and dignified people of Quraysh, while those influential people had risen against this new call with all their resources of wealth, numbers and family honour. And in a society in which no value other than lineage and honour and status was current, the talk was only this: "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, son of Hashim," and people would say:

"Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon some great man of the two towns?" (43:31)

The Messenger ﷺ was, among them, a man of noble lineage, yet he was not a chief, and they were merely worshippers of rank and power.

The truth is that in such a society only a prophet and divine revelation could bring about such a great revolution. No person living on the earth and thinking with a worldly mind could take such a revolutionary step, especially in the circumstances and at the time in which the Messenger ﷺ was carrying out the work of the Islamic call.

It was this heavenly power and heavenly guidance that directed this matter in this manner. This principle was enforced through the person of the Prophet ﷺ in those difficult circumstances. The Messenger ﷺ implemented it with great zeal, great strength and firmness, and he placed this constitution within the very foundations of the new society, and it remained established and enduring in the life of the Muslim community for a long period.

This was in truth a second birth for humanity, just as a human being is born in his natural state; indeed, this birth of humanity was in fact more precious. It meant that human society would bid farewell to the values current in some land and adopt values that are entirely new, revealed from the heavens. New ideas and new concepts would come, and these ideas, concepts, circumstances, practical relations and customs would be uprooted. People would be suddenly freed from the pressure of those former ideas and relations, and modern ideas and modern values would take root and settle within them. They would understand them well, and all of them would accept them, and this great revolution would come to pass. These modern values would be manifest in the conscience of the Muslim society and clear in its laws; then in reality this was a new birth for mankind. It was a great revolution, for the sake of bringing which even the person of Muhammad ﷺ needed admonition and guidance, and this revolution remained prominent in the life of the Muslims of the early period for a long time.

We people of the modern age indeed do not fully grasp this great revolution and this modern birth of humanity, because we have not abandoned the values of this world, its earthly relations and its outlook and theories, nor have we conformed ourselves to Islam. The domination of materialism, material values and worldly concepts over us is so great that some of the ignorant people of our age who put forward the materialist philosophy of history have come to think that beliefs, concepts, high values, sciences and arts arise as a result of material conditions and material and economic values. In the same way, they hold that all customs, traditions, principles and laws, which are in fact the product of economic values, are the outcome of these conditions. These people are extremely ignorant, and they are wholly unaware of the ups and downs of the human soul. In any case, the revolution that Islam brought about was a miracle and was a new birth for humanity.

After this new birth of humanity and this great revolution, these values prevailed over the atmosphere of the world, but their dominance in an Arab society was not so easy, nor was their establishment in the souls of the Muslims an easily attainable target. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, owing to his own excellences, then the will of Allah, then the guidance and direction from God, and then the eagerness of acting warmly upon the guidance of the Qur'an, implanted these great principles and values in the consciousness and conscience of the people. Like a plant, these new ethics and values were cultivated in their hearts, and then they were carefully guarded so that their roots would be firm. This is why centuries have passed over the Islamic society and yet these values remain firmly established, although in those centuries great storms of adverse winds have passed and countless factors have worked against these values.

After this event, whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met Ibn Umm Maktum, he would greet him with these words: "Welcome! It is by your sake that Allah, glorified is He, reproved me severely." The Messenger ﷺ appointed this blind poor man as governor of Madinah twice during his lifetime.

In Arab society, giving one's daughter in marriage was a matter of great sensitivity. In such matters, where a daughter was given, there was a strict standard for those people. The Prophet ﷺ had Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, his paternal cousin, married to his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah, so that a blow might be struck against those jahili values.

Earlier, when he established the system of brotherhood (mu'akhah) in Madinah, he made Zayd ibn Harithah, his freed slave, the brother of his own uncle Hamzah, and he made Bilal ibn Rabah the brother of Khalid ibn Ruwaymah al-Khath'ami.

He appointed Zayd as commander at the Battle of Mu'tah. He was the first commander of that expedition. After him the command was to pass to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and then to Abdullah ibn Rawahah al-Ansari. In that army were three thousand Ansar and Muhajirun, among whom was Khalid ibn al-Walid. The Prophet ﷺ himself went out to bid farewell to that army. In that battle all three of them were martyred. May Allah be pleased with them. And among the last commands of the Prophet ﷺ was this instruction: he appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as commander for the war against the Romans. In that army were countless Ansar and Muhajirun, among them Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, who were his companions and counsellors and who were the caliphs after him. Likewise, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was there, who was both among his close kin and one of the earliest Muslims of Quraysh.

Some people expressed surprise at the command of Usamah, because he was a very young man. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, narrates: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched an army and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as its commander. Some people objected to his command, so he said: 'If you find fault with the command of Usamah ibn Zayd, you had already objected to the command of his father before. By Allah, he was worthy of command, and he was among all people the most beloved to me, and this one is also the most beloved to me among all people.'" (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

And when some people spoke disparagingly of Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, and spoke in terms of Arab and Persian, and those remarks carried the smell of a limited Arab nationalism, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a decisive blow to that notion as well and said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." And the Muslims, through heavenly values, were carried beyond all the base worldly values, and in a moment they went beyond the horizons themselves, and the lines of limited nationality that were very important to the Arabs were erased, and Salman was declared a member of the People of the House. (Tabarani and Hakim)

When a dispute arose between Abu Dhar al-Ghifari and Bilal, may Allah be pleased with them, and the words "O son of a black woman" escaped the tongue of Abu Dhar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was greatly angered by it, and he flung the remark back into the face of Abu Dhar, saying: "Abu Dhar, keep your measure right; in Islam, the son of a white woman has no superiority over the son of a black woman." Thus he removed the matter from its very earliest roots. Islam is Islam, and it is founded on heavenly values; and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah, and its values are earthly. (Ibn al-Mubarak)

The words of the Messenger ﷺ had a severe effect on the sensitive heart of Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him. He placed his forehead upon the ground and swore that he would not raise his forehead until Bilal trampled it underfoot, for in his view that was the expiation for that wrong saying.

The scale by which Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, attained such weight was a heavenly scale. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bilal, tell me what deed you have done for which you expect a great reward from Allah, for I heard the sound of your sandals in Paradise on the night of the Mi'raj." He replied: "I have done nothing special, except that whenever I performed complete purification, by night or by day, after becoming Muslim, I then prayed as much as Allah had decreed for me. That is all, and by it I hope to receive greater reward." (Bukhari and Muslim)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, whenever he sought permission to meet the Prophet: "Admit him, for he is pure and purified." (Nasa'i) And on another occasion he said: "Ammar is full of faith from head to foot." Concerning Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "I do not know how long I shall remain among you, so follow these two after me" (pointing to Abu Bakr and Umar), "and follow the way of Ammar, and accept whatever Ibn Mas'ud tells you." (Tirmidhi)

As for Ibn Mas'ud, the condition was that when people who were not residents of Madinah came, they would take Ibn Mas'ud to be a man of the household of the Prophet ﷺ, because he frequently came and went and remained with the Messenger ﷺ at the right times. (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

There was a freed slave named Julaybib, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Messenger ﷺ himself sought a match for him. He wished that some woman from the Ansar might be found for him. When the Prophet ﷺ proposed to a girl on his behalf, her parents refused. The girl said: "Are you rejecting the word of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is pleased with this match, then give me in marriage to this man." Upon this her parents consented, and they gave the girl to him in marriage. (Ahmad)

This man was lost in battle shortly after his marriage. Abu Barzah al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took part in a military expedition (ghazwah). Allah granted him victory, and spoils of war (ghanimah) were obtained. After the battle, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked, "Do you find anyone missing?" The people said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so are not here." He then asked again, "Do you find anyone missing?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so are not here." He then said, "Is there anyone else missing?" They said, "No, nobody else is missing." He said, "Yes, I find Julaybib missing." The people searched for him, and he was found beside seven slain disbelievers. He had killed seven of them, and then they had killed him as a martyr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood by his body and said, "He killed seven, and then they killed him. He is mine and I am his. He is from me and I am from him." He then lifted him in his two arms. For him there was no bier other than the arms of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). A grave was dug for him, and he was placed in it. The narrator did not mention his being washed. (Muslim)

Through these guidance points from Allah, and because of the excellent example set by the Prophet (ﷺ), humanity was given a new birth. A society came into being in which the principles of good and evil were taken from the heavens. This society, although it existed on this very earth, was free from the base values of the earth. This was the great miracle of Islam. It was a great miracle, and no miracle can come about without the commands of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). This miracle shows that this religion was the religion of Allah, and the blessed person who presented this religion was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

After him, his second companion, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), became the leader of this religion. Of the two, this second Caliph understood this system better, followed the Sunnah of the noble Messenger (ﷺ) more closely, loved the Messenger, and walked in his footsteps in the field of love and obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Usamah felt shame that he should be riding while the elderly Caliph walked beside him, and he said, "O Caliph of the Muslims, either you ride or I will dismount." The Caliph of the Muslims swore an oath: "By Allah, you shall not dismount, and by Allah, I shall not ride. What would be the harm if my feet also became dusty in the path of Allah?"

This miracle could only happen by the will of Allah, and only a Messenger could bring it about.

The wheel of time turns, and there came a time when Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was Caliph, and he appointed Ammar ibn Yasir as governor of Kufa.

There came a time when Suhayl ibn Amr, Ibn al-Harith, Ibn Hisham and Abu Sufyan stood at the door of Umar's office, along with a group of the chiefs of Quraysh. These were people who had become Muslims after the conquest of Makkah and were called the "freed" (Tulaqa'). Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) first called Suhayb and Bilal inside, because they were among the foremost early converts (al-Sabiqun al-Awwalun) and among the people of Badr (Ahl Badr). Abu Sufyan's nostrils flared with anger, and in a highly emotional manner he said, "In my whole life I have never seen such a day, that these slaves are called inside while we are left at the door." His companions, who had grasped the reality of Islam and upon whose awareness Islam had prevailed, said to him, "O people, I can see the signs that have appeared on your faces. If you are feeling anger, then release this anger from your souls. These people were called to Islam, and you too were called. They responded immediately, and you delayed. Consider the time when they will be called on the Day of Resurrection and you will still be standing where you are." (Collective justice in Islam)

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) assigned Usamah ibn Zayd a stipend greater than that of Abdullah ibn Umar. Abdullah asked about the reason, and Umar replied, "Son, Zayd was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than your father, and Usamah was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than you. So I gave preference to the love of the Messenger of Allah over my own love." Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) knew that the love of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is measured by heavenly standards.

It is narrated that Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) bound him with his own cloak, and in some narrations it is said that he was bound with his turban. This continued until the investigation ended and, as a result, he was proven innocent. After this, Ammar released him, tied his turban on his head with his own hand, and Khalid (may Allah be pleased with him) felt no anger over this. This was because Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) was a companion of the noble Messenger (ﷺ) and one of the earliest to accept Islam, and Khalid knew what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said about him.

This is the criterion, the standard set by Allah. By it we must weigh the deeds and the intentions of others and of ourselves. This is the command of Allah, the word of Allah, and before it no word carries any weight; every act and every judgment is inferior to it.

Where was this command given, and where did this event occur? In Makkah, when the Islamic call was being pursued from every side, and the Muslims were very few in number. The Prophet ﷺ was not turning toward those influential people for any personal purpose, nor was his disregard of that blind man born of any personal motive. The sole concern before the Messenger ﷺ was the interest of the Islamic call, yet the scale of this call was different. Its values were different. It was to establish standards for people and to create traditions. This call could be successful, dignified and strong only if it set down such measures.

This was not merely an individual incident; it was a great principle. It was not a matter of ordinary moral conduct; rather, a fundamental and constitutional question was at hand: from where should people derive the standards of good and evil? From the customs of the earth or from heavenly guidance; from earthly and popular perspectives or from the presence of the Lord of Majesty, from where this principle has been laid down.

"Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the one most righteous among you" (49:13).

In this call and this movement, only that is significant which is significant in the sight of Allah, even if, in worldly terms, one is deprived of the factors that carry weight with people, such as lineage, numerical and financial strength, and other considerations that the world regards as important. If these things are devoid of faith and do not bear the colour of taqwa, they have no weight in this call. From the perspective of this movement, the important and foremost matter is that a person sets his circumstances right according to faith and taqwa.

Through this particular and individual incident, Allah intended to impress upon the minds of people this great truth and this great principle, in keeping with the Qur'anic method of reform and training, in which a great principle is drawn from an individual event and fixed in people's minds. The personality of Muhammad ﷺ was deeply affected by these instructions and by this reproof. He accepted these instructions with great zeal, and by acting upon them he put this principle and constitution into effect in the Islamic society. His first duty was determined to be that he himself should narrate this incident as a part of a Surah of the Qur'an. This was a momentous matter; only a Messenger of Allah could do it. From whatever aspect we consider it, a human being conceals his weaknesses. It was the Messenger of Allah alone who openly announced this divine reproof, and announced it in this unique manner. If there had been any leader other than a prophet, he would have become aware of his mistake and would have been more cautious in future, but the station of a prophet of Allah is of another kind. The horizons of the prophethood are of another kind, very lofty and far-reaching.

It was the Prophet alone who, in the most difficult and delicate circumstances, announced this principle before the influential and dignified people of Quraysh, while those influential people had risen against this new call with all their resources of wealth, numbers and family honour. And in a society in which no value other than lineage and honour and status was current, the talk was only this: "Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, son of Hashim," and people would say:

"Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon some great man of the two towns?" (43:31)

The Messenger ﷺ was, among them, a man of noble lineage, yet he was not a chief, and they were merely worshippers of rank and power.

The truth is that in such a society only a prophet and divine revelation could bring about such a great revolution. No person living on the earth and thinking with a worldly mind could take such a revolutionary step, especially in the circumstances and at the time in which the Messenger ﷺ was carrying out the work of the Islamic call.

It was this heavenly power and heavenly guidance that directed this matter in this manner. This principle was enforced through the person of the Prophet ﷺ in those difficult circumstances. The Messenger ﷺ implemented it with great zeal, great strength and firmness, and he placed this constitution within the very foundations of the new society, and it remained established and enduring in the life of the Muslim community for a long period.

This was in truth a second birth for humanity, just as a human being is born in his natural state; indeed, this birth of humanity was in fact more precious. It meant that human society would bid farewell to the values current in some land and adopt values that are entirely new, revealed from the heavens. New ideas and new concepts would come, and these ideas, concepts, circumstances, practical relations and customs would be uprooted. People would be suddenly freed from the pressure of those former ideas and relations, and modern ideas and modern values would take root and settle within them. They would understand them well, and all of them would accept them, and this great revolution would come to pass. These modern values would be manifest in the conscience of the Muslim society and clear in its laws; then in reality this was a new birth for mankind. It was a great revolution, for the sake of bringing which even the person of Muhammad ﷺ needed admonition and guidance, and this revolution remained prominent in the life of the Muslims of the early period for a long time.

We people of the modern age indeed do not fully grasp this great revolution and this modern birth of humanity, because we have not abandoned the values of this world, its earthly relations and its outlook and theories, nor have we conformed ourselves to Islam. The domination of materialism, material values and worldly concepts over us is so great that some of the ignorant people of our age who put forward the materialist philosophy of history have come to think that beliefs, concepts, high values, sciences and arts arise as a result of material conditions and material and economic values. In the same way, they hold that all customs, traditions, principles and laws, which are in fact the product of economic values, are the outcome of these conditions. These people are extremely ignorant, and they are wholly unaware of the ups and downs of the human soul. In any case, the revolution that Islam brought about was a miracle and was a new birth for humanity.

After this new birth of humanity and this great revolution, these values prevailed over the atmosphere of the world, but their dominance in an Arab society was not so easy, nor was their establishment in the souls of the Muslims an easily attainable target. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, owing to his own excellences, then the will of Allah, then the guidance and direction from God, and then the eagerness of acting warmly upon the guidance of the Qur'an, implanted these great principles and values in the consciousness and conscience of the people. Like a plant, these new ethics and values were cultivated in their hearts, and then they were carefully guarded so that their roots would be firm. This is why centuries have passed over the Islamic society and yet these values remain firmly established, although in those centuries great storms of adverse winds have passed and countless factors have worked against these values.

After this event, whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met Ibn Umm Maktum, he would greet him with these words: "Welcome! It is by your sake that Allah, glorified is He, reproved me severely." The Messenger ﷺ appointed this blind poor man as governor of Madinah twice during his lifetime.

In Arab society, giving one's daughter in marriage was a matter of great sensitivity. In such matters, where a daughter was given, there was a strict standard for those people. The Prophet ﷺ had Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, his paternal cousin, married to his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah, so that a blow might be struck against those jahili values.

Earlier, when he established the system of brotherhood (mu'akhah) in Madinah, he made Zayd ibn Harithah, his freed slave, the brother of his own uncle Hamzah, and he made Bilal ibn Rabah the brother of Khalid ibn Ruwaymah al-Khath'ami.

He appointed Zayd as commander at the Battle of Mu'tah. He was the first commander of that expedition. After him the command was to pass to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and then to Abdullah ibn Rawahah al-Ansari. In that army were three thousand Ansar and Muhajirun, among whom was Khalid ibn al-Walid. The Prophet ﷺ himself went out to bid farewell to that army. In that battle all three of them were martyred. May Allah be pleased with them. And among the last commands of the Prophet ﷺ was this instruction: he appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as commander for the war against the Romans. In that army were countless Ansar and Muhajirun, among them Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, who were his companions and counsellors and who were the caliphs after him. Likewise, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was there, who was both among his close kin and one of the earliest Muslims of Quraysh.

Some people expressed surprise at the command of Usamah, because he was a very young man. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, narrates: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched an army and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as its commander. Some people objected to his command, so he said: 'If you find fault with the command of Usamah ibn Zayd, you had already objected to the command of his father before. By Allah, he was worthy of command, and he was among all people the most beloved to me, and this one is also the most beloved to me among all people.'" (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

And when some people spoke disparagingly of Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, and spoke in terms of Arab and Persian, and those remarks carried the smell of a limited Arab nationalism, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a decisive blow to that notion as well and said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." And the Muslims, through heavenly values, were carried beyond all the base worldly values, and in a moment they went beyond the horizons themselves, and the lines of limited nationality that were very important to the Arabs were erased, and Salman was declared a member of the People of the House. (Tabarani and Hakim)

When a dispute arose between Abu Dhar al-Ghifari and Bilal, may Allah be pleased with them, and the words "O son of a black woman" escaped the tongue of Abu Dhar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was greatly angered by it, and he flung the remark back into the face of Abu Dhar, saying: "Abu Dhar, keep your measure right; in Islam, the son of a white woman has no superiority over the son of a black woman." Thus he removed the matter from its very earliest roots. Islam is Islam, and it is founded on heavenly values; and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah, and its values are earthly. (Ibn al-Mubarak)

The words of the Messenger ﷺ had a severe effect on the sensitive heart of Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him. He placed his forehead upon the ground and swore that he would not raise his forehead until Bilal trampled it underfoot, for in his view that was the expiation for that wrong saying.

The scale by which Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, attained such weight was a heavenly scale. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bilal, tell me what deed you have done for which you expect a great reward from Allah, for I heard the sound of your sandals in Paradise on the night of the Mi'raj." He replied: "I have done nothing special, except that whenever I performed complete purification, by night or by day, after becoming Muslim, I then prayed as much as Allah had decreed for me. That is all, and by it I hope to receive greater reward." (Bukhari and Muslim)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, whenever he sought permission to meet the Prophet: "Admit him, for he is pure and purified." (Nasa'i) And on another occasion he said: "Ammar is full of faith from head to foot." Concerning Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "I do not know how long I shall remain among you, so follow these two after me" (pointing to Abu Bakr and Umar), "and follow the way of Ammar, and accept whatever Ibn Mas'ud tells you." (Tirmidhi)

As for Ibn Mas'ud, the condition was that when people who were not residents of Madinah came, they would take Ibn Mas'ud to be a man of the household of the Prophet ﷺ, because he frequently came and went and remained with the Messenger ﷺ at the right times. (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

There was a freed slave named Julaybib, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Messenger ﷺ himself sought a match for him. He wished that some woman from the Ansar might be found for him. When the Prophet ﷺ proposed to a girl on his behalf, her parents refused. The girl said: "Are you rejecting the word of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is pleased with this match, then give me in marriage to this man." Upon this her parents consented, and they gave the girl to him in marriage. (Ahmad)

This man was lost in battle shortly after his marriage. Abu Barzah al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took part in a military expedition (ghazwah). Allah granted him victory, and spoils of war (ghanimah) were obtained. After the battle, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked, "Do you find anyone missing?" The people said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so are not here." He then asked again, "Do you find anyone missing?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so are not here." He then said, "Is there anyone else missing?" They said, "No, nobody else is missing." He said, "Yes, I find Julaybib missing." The people searched for him, and he was found beside seven slain disbelievers. He had killed seven of them, and then they had killed him as a martyr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood by his body and said, "He killed seven, and then they killed him. He is mine and I am his. He is from me and I am from him." He then lifted him in his two arms. For him there was no bier other than the arms of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). A grave was dug for him, and he was placed in it. The narrator did not mention his being washed. (Muslim)

Through these guidance points from Allah, and because of the excellent example set by the Prophet (ﷺ), humanity was given a new birth. A society came into being in which the principles of good and evil were taken from the heavens. This society, although it existed on this very earth, was free from the base values of the earth. This was the great miracle of Islam. It was a great miracle, and no miracle can come about without the commands of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). This miracle shows that this religion was the religion of Allah, and the blessed person who presented this religion was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Allah also had a special plan: after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his first companion, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), became the ruler and Caliph of the Muslims (Khalifat al-Muslimin). After him, his second companion, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), became the leader of this religion. Of the two, this second Caliph understood this system better, followed the Sunnah of the noble Messenger (ﷺ) more closely, loved the Messenger, and walked in his footsteps in the field of love and obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) had understood the insistence of the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding Usamah. Therefore, after taking up the office of command (imarah), the first thing he did was to fulfil this task. This army had been prepared by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), the Caliph of the Muslims, bade it farewell outside Madinah himself. Usamah was riding, and Abu Bakr, the Caliph of the Muslims, was walking alongside his mount on foot. Usamah felt shame that he should be riding while the elderly Caliph walked beside him, and he said, "O Caliph of the Muslims, either you ride or I will dismount." The Caliph of the Muslims swore an oath: "By Allah, you shall not dismount, and by Allah, I shall not ride. What would be the harm if my feet also became dusty in the path of Allah?"

After this, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) thought that he needed Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), since the burden of the Caliphate had fallen upon his shoulders, but Umar was merely one soldier in the army of Usamah, and Usamah was the commander. Therefore it was necessary to seek permission from Usamah. So he said, "If you think it appropriate, and if you can, let Umar go and help me." Look at the words: "If you think it appropriate, let Umar go and help me." These are the heights to which Islam raised human beings. This miracle could only happen by the will of Allah, and only a Messenger could bring it about.

The wheel of time turns, and there came a time when Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was Caliph, and he appointed Ammar ibn Yasir as governor of Kufa.

There came a time when Suhayl ibn Amr, Ibn al-Harith, Ibn Hisham and Abu Sufyan stood at the door of Umar's office, along with a group of the chiefs of Quraysh. These were people who had become Muslims after the conquest of Makkah and were called the "freed" (Tulaqa'). Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) first called Suhayb and Bilal inside, because they were among the foremost early converts (al-Sabiqun al-Awwalun) and among the people of Badr (Ahl Badr). Abu Sufyan's nostrils flared with anger, and in a highly emotional manner he said, "In my whole life I have never seen such a day, that these slaves are called inside while we are left at the door." His companions, who had grasped the reality of Islam and upon whose awareness Islam had prevailed, said to him, "O people, I can see the signs that have appeared on your faces. If you are feeling anger, then release this anger from your souls. These people were called to Islam, and you too were called. They responded immediately, and you delayed. Consider the time when they will be called on the Day of Resurrection and you will still be standing where you are." (Collective justice in Islam)

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) assigned Usamah ibn Zayd a stipend greater than that of Abdullah ibn Umar. Abdullah asked about the reason, and Umar replied, "Son, Zayd was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than your father, and Usamah was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than you. So I gave preference to the love of the Messenger of Allah over my own love." Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) knew that the love of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is measured by heavenly standards.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) sent Ammar ibn Yasir to investigate certain complaints against Khalid ibn al-Walid, the great commander of Islam, its conqueror, and a member of a noble family. It is narrated that Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) bound him with his own cloak, and in some narrations it is said that he was bound with his turban. This continued until the investigation ended and, as a result, he was proven innocent. After this, Ammar released him, tied his turban on his head with his own hand, and Khalid (may Allah be pleased with him) felt no anger over this. This was because Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) was a companion of the noble Messenger (ﷺ) and one of the earliest to accept Islam, and Khalid knew what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said about him.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say about Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "He is our chief, who freed our other chief from slavery, that is, Bilal, who was a slave of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and Umayyah used to subject him to severe torment. Abu Bakr bought him and set him free." About him Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Bilal is our chief."

It was Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) who said, "If Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, were alive, I would have made him Caliph." On the one hand Umar says this, and on the other hand he did not make Uthman, Ali, Talhah and Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them all) Caliphs. Instead, he appointed a consultative council (Shura) of six men, so that one of them would be chosen.

Ali, Ammar and Hasan ibn Ali were sent to the people of Kufa. They requested that the people support them in the dispute that had arisen with Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her). Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I know well that Aisha is the wife of your Prophet (ﷺ), both in this world and in the Hereafter, but Allah has put you to the test to see whether you obey me or her." (Bukhari) In this way, people listened to what she said about her.

Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) was the governor of Yemen. Abu Ruwayhah al-Khath'ami wished to marry into a tribe in Yemen. He requested that Bilal recommend him. Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I am Bilal ibn Rabah, and this is my brother Abu Ruwayhah. This man does not have good manners, nor is he very religious. If you wish, give your daughter to him in marriage, and if you do not wish, then do not." Bilal did not deceive them, nor did he conceal anything about this man, nor did he say that he was merely a recommender. He only kept in view that whatever he said, he would be held accountable before Allah. People saw how sincere these men were, and they gave the girl in marriage. They considered it enough that he was an Arab of noble lineage, and that his sincere recommendation was being made by Bilal, the Abyssinian.

In short, this great reality was established in practice within the Islamic society, and it remained in place for a long time afterward. Although, in the periods that followed, many factors of decline and deterioration appeared among the Muslims. Whenever Abdullah ibn Abbas is mentioned, his freed slave Ikrimah is also mentioned alongside him. Whenever Abdullah ibn Umar is mentioned, his slave Nafi' is also mentioned. Ibn Sirin is mentioned alongside Anas ibn Malik, and Abu Hurayrah is mentioned together with his slave Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmuz. In Basra, Hasan al-Basri, in Makkah, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and Tawus ibn Kaysan were famous jurists (fuqaha). In the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, in Egypt, Yazid ibn Abi Habib was appointed Grand Mufti. He was a dark-skinned freed slave of Alqamah.

These were the heavenly and Islamic values which raised humanity to such heights on the basis of taqwa (God-consciousness), even though they possessed none of the qualities that are most esteemed in the world, neither in their own persons nor in their surroundings. These balances and standards remained in the world until the recent past. In the recent past, jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) once again covered the whole world. A part of the world came under American jahiliyyah, in which human worth began to be determined in the form of the dollar, and leadership of half the eastern world came to Russian jahiliyyah, in which a human being was worth nothing more than a productive machine. As for the Islamic world, it was covered by the same jahiliyyah, namely Arab nationalist jahiliyyah, which Islam had come to uproot from its foundations, and in practice Islam had uprooted it and cast it away. Today, this high standard and high value has been erased from the Islamic world, and the Islamic world has sunk into the darkness of a jahiliyyah in which faith and taqwa are not even considered high values.

Yes, in the Islamic world the movement of Islamic call (da'wah) and the revival of Islam (ihya' al-Islam) is ongoing. Our only hope is in this movement, that it will bring the whole world out of jahiliyyah and give it once again heavenly values, and perhaps humanity will once more be reborn, as it was in the early period of Islam. A glimpse of this is shown in the opening verses of this surah. These are a few verses, but they are extremely important, a milestone, and decisive.

In commenting on a particular event, the first part of the surah stated this great reality. In this second part, there is expressed great astonishment at the attitude of the human being who turns away from such truths and from this call to faith and taqwa, and who regards himself as superior and above the call of Islam. If this person reflected on his origin and the circumstances of his creation, he would certainly not turn away. The human being does not see the many favours of Allah upon him. His life is under the control of Allah at every step, and in this world and the Hereafter, this human being is in fact in the power of Allah at every stage of life. Yet he does not fulfil the rights of his Creator, his Sustainer and his Reckoner, and he does not fear Him.

This is why centuries have passed over the Islamic society and yet these values remain firmly established, although in those centuries great storms of adverse winds have passed and countless factors have worked against these values.

After this event, whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met Ibn Umm Maktum, he would greet him with these words: "Welcome! It is by your sake that Allah, glorified is He, reproved me severely." The Messenger ﷺ appointed this blind poor man as governor of Madinah twice during his lifetime.

In Arab society, giving one's daughter in marriage was a matter of great sensitivity. In such matters, where a daughter was given, there was a strict standard for those people. The Prophet ﷺ had Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, his paternal cousin, married to his freed slave Zayd ibn Harithah, so that a blow might be struck against those jahili values.

Earlier, when he established the system of brotherhood (mu'akhah) in Madinah, he made Zayd ibn Harithah, his freed slave, the brother of his own uncle Hamzah, and he made Bilal ibn Rabah the brother of Khalid ibn Ruwaymah al-Khath'ami.

He appointed Zayd as commander at the Battle of Mu'tah. He was the first commander of that expedition. After him the command was to pass to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and then to Abdullah ibn Rawahah al-Ansari. In that army were three thousand Ansar and Muhajirun, among whom was Khalid ibn al-Walid. The Prophet ﷺ himself went out to bid farewell to that army. In that battle all three of them were martyred. May Allah be pleased with them. And among the last commands of the Prophet ﷺ was this instruction: he appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as commander for the war against the Romans. In that army were countless Ansar and Muhajirun, among them Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, who were his companions and counsellors and who were the caliphs after him. Likewise, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was there, who was both among his close kin and one of the earliest Muslims of Quraysh.

Some people expressed surprise at the command of Usamah, because he was a very young man. Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, narrates: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched an army and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as its commander. Some people objected to his command, so he said: 'If you find fault with the command of Usamah ibn Zayd, you had already objected to the command of his father before. By Allah, he was worthy of command, and he was among all people the most beloved to me, and this one is also the most beloved to me among all people.'" (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

And when some people spoke disparagingly of Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, and spoke in terms of Arab and Persian, and those remarks carried the smell of a limited Arab nationalism, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a decisive blow to that notion as well and said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." And the Muslims, through heavenly values, were carried beyond all the base worldly values, and in a moment they went beyond the horizons themselves, and the lines of limited nationality that were very important to the Arabs were erased, and Salman was declared a member of the People of the House. (Tabarani and Hakim)

When a dispute arose between Abu Dhar al-Ghifari and Bilal, may Allah be pleased with them, and the words "O son of a black woman" escaped the tongue of Abu Dhar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was greatly angered by it, and he flung the remark back into the face of Abu Dhar, saying: "Abu Dhar, keep your measure right; in Islam, the son of a white woman has no superiority over the son of a black woman." Thus he removed the matter from its very earliest roots. Islam is Islam, and it is founded on heavenly values; and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah, and its values are earthly. (Ibn al-Mubarak)

The words of the Messenger ﷺ had a severe effect on the sensitive heart of Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him. He placed his forehead upon the ground and swore that he would not raise his forehead until Bilal trampled it underfoot, for in his view that was the expiation for that wrong saying.

The scale by which Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, attained such weight was a heavenly scale. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bilal, tell me what deed you have done for which you expect a great reward from Allah, for I heard the sound of your sandals in Paradise on the night of the Mi'raj." He replied: "I have done nothing special, except that whenever I performed complete purification, by night or by day, after becoming Muslim, I then prayed as much as Allah had decreed for me. That is all, and by it I hope to receive greater reward." (Bukhari and Muslim)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, whenever he sought permission to meet the Prophet: "Admit him, for he is pure and purified." (Nasa'i) And on another occasion he said: "Ammar is full of faith from head to foot." Concerning Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "I do not know how long I shall remain among you, so follow these two after me" (pointing to Abu Bakr and Umar), "and follow the way of Ammar, and accept whatever Ibn Mas'ud tells you." (Tirmidhi)

As for Ibn Mas'ud, the condition was that when people who were not residents of Madinah came, they would take Ibn Mas'ud to be a man of the household of the Prophet ﷺ, because he frequently came and went and remained with the Messenger ﷺ at the right times. (Bukhari, Muslim and Tirmidhi)

There was a freed slave named Julaybib, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Messenger ﷺ himself sought a match for him. He wished that some woman from the Ansar might be found for him. When the Prophet ﷺ proposed to a girl on his behalf, her parents refused. The girl said: "Are you rejecting the word of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is pleased with this match, then give me in marriage to this man." Upon this her parents consented, and they gave the girl to him in marriage. (Ahmad)

This man was lost in battle shortly after his marriage. Abu Barzah al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took part in a military expedition (ghazwah). Allah granted him victory, and spoils of war (ghanimah) were obtained. After the battle, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked, "Do you find anyone missing?" The people said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so are not here." He then asked again, "Do you find anyone missing?" They said, "Yes, so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so are not here." He then said, "Is there anyone else missing?" They said, "No, nobody else is missing." He said, "Yes, I find Julaybib missing." The people searched for him, and he was found beside seven slain disbelievers. He had killed seven of them, and then they had killed him as a martyr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood by his body and said, "He killed seven, and then they killed him. He is mine and I am his. He is from me and I am from him." He then lifted him in his two arms. For him there was no bier other than the arms of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). A grave was dug for him, and he was placed in it. The narrator did not mention his being washed. (Muslim)

Through these guidance points from Allah, and because of the excellent example set by the Prophet (ﷺ), humanity was given a new birth. A society came into being in which the principles of good and evil were taken from the heavens. This society, although it existed on this very earth, was free from the base values of the earth. This was the great miracle of Islam. It was a great miracle, and no miracle can come about without the commands of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). This miracle shows that this religion was the religion of Allah, and the blessed person who presented this religion was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Allah also had a special plan: after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his first companion, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), became the ruler and Caliph of the Muslims (Khalifat al-Muslimin). After him, his second companion, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), became the leader of this religion. Of the two, this second Caliph understood this system better, followed the Sunnah of the noble Messenger (ﷺ) more closely, loved the Messenger, and walked in his footsteps in the field of love and obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) had understood the insistence of the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding Usamah. Therefore, after taking up the office of command (imarah), the first thing he did was to fulfil this task. This army had been prepared by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), the Caliph of the Muslims, bade it farewell outside Madinah himself. Usamah was riding, and Abu Bakr, the Caliph of the Muslims, was walking alongside his mount on foot. Usamah felt shame that he should be riding while the elderly Caliph walked beside him, and he said, "O Caliph of the Muslims, either you ride or I will dismount." The Caliph of the Muslims swore an oath: "By Allah, you shall not dismount, and by Allah, I shall not ride. What would be the harm if my feet also became dusty in the path of Allah?"

After this, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) thought that he needed Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), since the burden of the Caliphate had fallen upon his shoulders, but Umar was merely one soldier in the army of Usamah, and Usamah was the commander. Therefore it was necessary to seek permission from Usamah. So he said, "If you think it appropriate, and if you can, let Umar go and help me." Look at the words: "If you think it appropriate, let Umar go and help me." These are the heights to which Islam raised human beings. This miracle could only happen by the will of Allah, and only a Messenger could bring it about.

The wheel of time turns, and there came a time when Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was Caliph, and he appointed Ammar ibn Yasir as governor of Kufa.

There came a time when Suhayl ibn Amr, Ibn al-Harith, Ibn Hisham and Abu Sufyan stood at the door of Umar's office, along with a group of the chiefs of Quraysh. These were people who had become Muslims after the conquest of Makkah and were called the "freed" (Tulaqa'). Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) first called Suhayb and Bilal inside, because they were among the foremost early converts (al-Sabiqun al-Awwalun) and among the people of Badr (Ahl Badr). Abu Sufyan's nostrils flared with anger, and in a highly emotional manner he said, "In my whole life I have never seen such a day, that these slaves are called inside while we are left at the door." His companions, who had grasped the reality of Islam and upon whose awareness Islam had prevailed, said to him, "O people, I can see the signs that have appeared on your faces. If you are feeling anger, then release this anger from your souls. These people were called to Islam, and you too were called. They responded immediately, and you delayed. Consider the time when they will be called on the Day of Resurrection and you will still be standing where you are." (Collective justice in Islam)

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) assigned Usamah ibn Zayd a stipend greater than that of Abdullah ibn Umar. Abdullah asked about the reason, and Umar replied, "Son, Zayd was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than your father, and Usamah was dearer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than you. So I gave preference to the love of the Messenger of Allah over my own love." Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) knew that the love of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is measured by heavenly standards.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) sent Ammar ibn Yasir to investigate certain complaints against Khalid ibn al-Walid, the great commander of Islam, its conqueror, and a member of a noble family. It is narrated that Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) bound him with his own cloak, and in some narrations it is said that he was bound with his turban. This continued until the investigation ended and, as a result, he was proven innocent. After this, Ammar released him, tied his turban on his head with his own hand, and Khalid (may Allah be pleased with him) felt no anger over this. This was because Ammar (may Allah be pleased with him) was a companion of the noble Messenger (ﷺ) and one of the earliest to accept Islam, and Khalid knew what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said about him.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say about Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "He is our chief, who freed our other chief from slavery, that is, Bilal, who was a slave of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and Umayyah used to subject him to severe torment. Abu Bakr bought him and set him free." About him Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Bilal is our chief."

It was Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) who said, "If Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, were alive, I would have made him Caliph." On the one hand Umar says this, and on the other hand he did not make Uthman, Ali, Talhah and Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them all) Caliphs. Instead, he appointed a consultative council (Shura) of six men, so that one of them would be chosen.

Ali, Ammar and Hasan ibn Ali were sent to the people of Kufa. They requested that the people support them in the dispute that had arisen with Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her). Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I know well that Aisha is the wife of your Prophet (ﷺ), both in this world and in the Hereafter, but Allah has put you to the test to see whether you obey me or her." (Bukhari) In this way, people listened to what she said about her.

Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) was the governor of Yemen. Abu Ruwayhah al-Khath'ami wished to marry into a tribe in Yemen. He requested that Bilal recommend him. Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I am Bilal ibn Rabah, and this is my brother Abu Ruwayhah. This man does not have good manners, nor is he very religious. If you wish, give your daughter to him in marriage, and if you do not wish, then do not." Bilal did not deceive them, nor did he conceal anything about this man, nor did he say that he was merely a recommender. He only kept in view that whatever he said, he would be held accountable before Allah. People saw how sincere these men were, and they gave the girl in marriage. They considered it enough that he was an Arab of noble lineage, and that his sincere recommendation was being made by Bilal, the Abyssinian.

In short, this great reality was established in practice within the Islamic society, and it remained in place for a long time afterward. Although, in the periods that followed, many factors of decline and deterioration appeared among the Muslims. Whenever Abdullah ibn Abbas is mentioned, his freed slave Ikrimah is also mentioned alongside him. Whenever Abdullah ibn Umar is mentioned, his slave Nafi' is also mentioned. Ibn Sirin is mentioned alongside Anas ibn Malik, and Abu Hurayrah is mentioned together with his slave Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmuz. In Basra, Hasan al-Basri, in Makkah, Mujahid, Ata ibn Abi Rabah and Tawus ibn Kaysan were famous jurists (fuqaha). In the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, in Egypt, Yazid ibn Abi Habib was appointed Grand Mufti. He was a dark-skinned freed slave of Alqamah.

These were the heavenly and Islamic values which raised humanity to such heights on the basis of taqwa (God-consciousness), even though they possessed none of the qualities that are most esteemed in the world, neither in their own persons nor in their surroundings. These balances and standards remained in the world until the recent past. In the recent past, jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) once again covered the whole world. A part of the world came under American jahiliyyah, in which human worth began to be determined in the form of the dollar, and leadership of half the eastern world came to Russian jahiliyyah, in which a human being was worth nothing more than a productive machine. As for the Islamic world, it was covered by the same jahiliyyah, namely Arab nationalist jahiliyyah, which Islam had come to uproot from its foundations, and in practice Islam had uprooted it and cast it away. Today, this high standard and high value has been erased from the Islamic world, and the Islamic world has sunk into the darkness of a jahiliyyah in which faith and taqwa are not even considered high values.

Yes, in the Islamic world the movement of Islamic call (da'wah) and the revival of Islam (ihya' al-Islam) is ongoing. Our only hope is in this movement, that it will bring the whole world out of jahiliyyah and give it once again heavenly values, and perhaps humanity will once more be reborn, as it was in the early period of Islam. A glimpse of this is shown in the opening verses of this surah. These are a few verses, but they are extremely important, a milestone, and decisive.

In commenting on a particular event, the first part of the surah stated this great reality. In this second part, there is expressed great astonishment at the attitude of the human being who turns away from such truths and from this call to faith and taqwa, and who regards himself as superior and above the call of Islam. If this person reflected on his origin and the circumstances of his creation, he would certainly not turn away. The human being does not see the many favours of Allah upon him. His life is under the control of Allah at every step, and in this world and the Hereafter, this human being is in fact in the power of Allah at every stage of life. Yet he does not fulfil the rights of his Creator, his Sustainer and his Reckoner, and he does not fear Him.

"Qutilal-insanu" (80:17): "Let man be destroyed." It is a rebuke and a manner of reproach: man deserves to be killed for these astonishing deeds of his. The meaning is that what man is doing is so evil that if he were given the death penalty for it, it would be no cause for wonder.

"Ma akfarahu" (80:17): "How ungrateful he is!" He is extremely intense in disbelief and denial. If he had reflected upon his own creation, he would have given thanks to his Creator. He would have adopted humility in the world and kept the Hereafter in mind. What is this man so pleased about? He considers himself unconcerned, and turns away from guidance. Let him just reflect upon his own origin and the circumstances of the beginning of his existence.

From what thing did He create him? (80:18) From a meager drop. Its origin is extremely ordinary, humble and insignificant. It is by the grace and generosity of Allah alone that, through His decree and planning, He has made a human being from that germ.

From a drop of seminal fluid He created him, then ordained his measure. (80:19) That is: from a drop that has no value and from a base germ that has no power of its own, he could not have come into being by himself; it was the Creator who decreed his coming into existence. Then He gave strength and firmness to his formation and creation. Then He made him a healthy and vigorous creature, gave him preference over all creatures and made him honoured, and appointed this lowly germ as master on this earth.

Then ... [He] made the way easy for him (80:20). The way of life, or the way of guidance. He endowed him with the capacity and abilities to walk along the way of life, or the paths of guidance. And when this journey of life ended, this human being too reached the end that every living creature must reach. He has no power to halt at that end, and there is no way of escape from that end.

Then ... "then He caused him to die and put him in a grave" (80:21). Just as his coming is by the command of Allah, so too is his end by the command of Allah. When Allah wills, He brings him into life, and when He wills, He ends the course of his life and places him in the belly of the grave. This grave too He has appointed for him out of regard for his dignity and as a mercy upon him. He did not leave him to be cast away wherever he dies, to be torn apart by beasts. He placed in human nature the disposition that the bodies of dead people be hidden in the grave. This too is part of Allah's plan, decree and commands, that the dead be buried. And when the time of accountability arrives, according to Allah's will, he will be raised again from the earth, and this too will be by Allah's command.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 80, verse 22:

"Then when He wills, He will raise him up again" (80:22). For he is not left aimless, nor will he be allowed to become part of the earth without any reckoning and account. So reflect: is this human being making any preparation for that very reckoning? Consider whether or not this human being is making any preparation for that very reckoning.

"Nay, (man) has not fulfilled what He commanded him." (80:23)

The subject here is man in general. Every individual of mankind, in every age, falls short in carrying out the commands of Allah, and this is their way throughout their whole lives. The particle "lamma" (not yet / has not) points to this meaning. Nay, man is at fault in every circumstance: he does not discharge his duties, and he does not keep before his eyes his own origin and reality, though this should be before him at all times. Moreover, he does not render the due thanks to his Creator, his Guide and his Sustainer. And he does not traverse the brief journey of this life in such a way that his actions are based on keeping the Hereafter in view. On the whole, the condition of man is such that the majority are disobedient, ungrateful, indifferent to guidance, and arrogant.

Now a new paragraph begins. The previous paragraph dealt with the creation of man; now it is said that man should just reflect upon his own food and that of his cattle. Consider what provision Allah has made in this worldly life and journey for man and his cattle. For man's reflection, this one thing that Allah has provided for him is sufficient.

This is the story of man and the food of his livestock, every stage of whose preparation has been stated here in brief. Man should reflect upon it. Does he have any part at all in these arrangements? Is all of this taking place by his own planning? The Being who created him and brought him into this world and onto this earth is the same Being who made all these arrangements.

﴿Then let man look at his food﴾ (80:24). This system of sustenance is directly connected with him, close to him, inseparable from him. He should reflect upon this present, ever-existing and constantly recurring system. Its story and its account are both remarkably wondrous and remarkably simple. Because this process goes on with such ease, the marvels and perfections within it escape the eye. In truth, this system of provision is as much a miracle as the creation of man is a miracle. Just as every stage of creation lies in the hand of Allah, so too every stage of this system of sustenance lies within the power of Allah's dominion.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 80, verse 25:

﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا﴾ (80:25) "We pour down water in abundance." The pouring down of water in the form of rain is a phenomenon with which people of every age have been familiar. Humans at the earliest and the most advanced stages of knowledge and experience were acquainted with it. It is a reality placed before every human being, but when humanity progressed, it came to know what breadths of meaning this verse contains. Among the hypotheses that today's environmental experts put forward regarding this gathering of water upon the earth, the closest to the truth is that this water was in the atmosphere above us, fell to the earth in the form of rain, and took the shape of seas.

One of the scientists of the present age says: "If we accept that at the time of its separation from the sun, the temperature of the earth, or the temperature of the earth's surface, was approximately 12,000 degrees, then it must be admitted that at that time all the elements were separate from one another and there was no possibility of any chemical combination. Then the globe and its constituent parts gradually cooled, and in this way various chemical compounds came into existence, and the debris of this world came into being which we know. Oxygen and hydrogen cannot combine until the temperature reaches 4000 thousand degrees Fahrenheit. Thus, when the temperature came down to 4000 thousand degrees Fahrenheit, these elements combined and water came into existence, and modern science has determined that it was in the form of an atmospheric envelope, and the water of the sea was not on the earth but in the form of air. And all the other elements were also simple, their combination had not yet taken place. These elements were in the form of gases. When water was produced in the atmospheric envelope, it began to fall to the earth, but as this rain approached the earth, due to the greater heat it would again turn into gas and rise into the atmosphere, because the temperature of the earth was even higher than that of the upper atmospheres thousands of miles away. Eventually, as the earth gradually cooled, this storm of rains reached near the earth and, due to the heat, kept rising again as vapour. At last, this great storm cooled the surface of the earth, and these great seas which were in the atmospheres were brought down onto the earth. How immense these storms were is hard even to imagine." (Ilm Imaan ki tarah hota hai, translated by Dr. Mahmood Salih Falaki)

We regard these hypotheses and theories only as hypotheses, and we do not confine the Qur'an to them. Yet these theories widen the meaning of the Qur'an and bring it closer to our understanding and comprehension. This is in fact the scientific history of pouring down water. These theories are, after all, theories. They may be correct or they may be incorrect. It is also possible that in future other theories about the descent of water to the earth will come into existence, because the Qur'an addresses people of every age and every standard of knowledge. And this is the miracle of the Qur'an, that every person believes that it has been understood by him alone.

This was the first part of the food (ta'am).

﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا﴾ (80:25) "We pour down water in abundance." Can a human think that he has any part in the creation of this water, or any role in the history of its origin, or that humans, by some device, poured these seas onto the earth so that they might arrange their food?

Then (We) split the earth in a wondrous manner (Qur'an 80:26). This is the third stage after the pouring of water. This matter was understood even by primitive, Stone Age man, who saw that water was falling from the heavens, that it was falling by the power of God, and that human planning and destiny had no part in it. After this, he saw that it entered the soil by splitting the earth, or he saw that the soil of the earth was split by the power of God. From this, vegetation emerges and rises into the atmosphere. Yet this vegetation ? ? ? ? page number 839 ? ? ? ? and the earth is extremely heavy and firm, but it is the hand of divine power that, by splitting this firm earth, helps bring out the soft and delicate plant from within it. This too is a miracle that everyone sees who has observed plants and soil. From this it is known that a hidden power is at work within this universe, and that it is an extremely merciful power.

But after this initial meaning, when the sciences that follow are studied, the scope of the meaning and implication of the verse expands. And the splitting of the earth may also mean that it has been made suitable for the nurturing of plants. As we stated in the previous discussion, terrible floods of water came upon the earth, and as a result the rocks of the earth's crust were broken up and washed away, and level plains came into being, within which soil suitable for cultivation accumulated. This meaning is also included in this verse.

Then (We) split the earth (Qur'an 80:26): the verse.

It comes after: We poured down water (Qur'an 80:25). This too points to the same thing: that the splitting of the earth followed the water.

In any case, whether this is the meaning of these verses or some third meaning, in the third stage of investigation there is mention of the creation of vegetation, and apparently it refers to the plants that serve as fodder for humans and for the livestock that benefit humans, and which even early man understood well.
﴿Then We caused grain to grow therein﴾ (80:27). By this is meant all vegetation, which humans use in one form or another, and which livestock use in one form or another as their food.
"And grapes and herbs" (80:28). Grapes are well known. Qadb (قضب) refers to those plants eaten as vegetables, which are cut and gathered again and again.

And olives and date-palms, and dense gardens, and fruits and fodder. The olive and the date-palm are well known. "Hada'iq" is the plural of "hadiqah", which denotes a fruit-bearing garden enclosed within walls. "Ghulban" is the plural of "ghalba'", meaning gardens whose trees are dense and whose branches have intertwined with one another.

"Hada'iq" is the plural of "hadiqah", which denotes a fruit-bearing garden enclosed within walls. "Ghulban" is the plural of "ghalba'", meaning gardens whose trees are dense and whose branches have intertwined with one another.

**Fruit**: the fruit that gardens yield to it.

The meaning of *abba* (80:31) is probably that which people cultivate and tend for fodder. Regarding its meaning, Ḥaḍrat ʿUmar (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) was asked, and he reproached himself, as has passed in Surah al-Nāziʿāt.

This was the account of human food. All the requirements of human sustenance are provided by Allah alone, and man has no part in it. Not only does man have no part in it, but man does not even claim to have a part in any of its various stages. Even in the growth of the seed that he sows in the earth, he has no part. Man neither created the seed nor invented it. How these living things were originally brought into being is a miracle, and man is beyond conception and comprehension. This soil is before man and is one, and every grain, in the same earth and in adjoining plots, brings forth its own fruit and flowers, while the same water and other elements nourish it. Yet it is precisely the decree of power that plants and fruits differ. And the seeds that come forth from these plants and fruits contain all the characteristics of the "mother seed." These matters and this technology are hidden from man. No one knows its secret, nor can anyone make a decision in it, nor is anyone consulted about it. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 80, verse 32:

"A provision for you and your cattle" (80:32): as a means of enjoyment for you and your livestock, for a fixed term. When this world comes to an end, this provision too will end, because Allah has made it a means of enjoyment for life. After that there will be another great event. What will it be? A person should reflect upon it before it takes place.

This is the end of the worldly apparatus. It accords with Allah's long-range plan and His comprehensive and integrated arrangement, according to which Allah created man in stages, advanced him in line with that plan, and thus his end corresponds exactly to his beginning. This will be the state of all people on that Day when this Sound is raised. It will be a harsh and piercing sound, such that the ears will be deafened. What will be the condition of the believers that Day, and what will be the condition of the disbelievers? On that Day, all will be measured by the measures of Allah and weighed by the scales of Allah.

"Some faces on that Day will be radiant, laughing and joyful" (39).

They will have been saved from the fear of that harsh, dreadful sound. "Those are the disbelievers and the wicked." (80:42) These are the people who did not believe in Allah and His messengers, and who transgressed the limits set by Allah.

There will be two kinds of faces, and the end of two kinds of people is shown within these two faces in the manner in which one sees one's own face in a mirror. The features of the faces have been portrayed in words and expressions in such a way that it is as if the faces, passing before the eyes, are clearly visible. This is the forceful style of expression of the Qur'an and its literary touch.

With this end, the beginning and the end of the surah also come into harmony with each other. At the beginning there was mention of Islamic values, and at the end the fate of people is described according to Islamic measures and the Islamic scale. Thus in this very short surah great realities have been brought, excellent scenes have been presented, and excellent guidance and indications have been given, and this surah, with its beautiful style of expression, delivers its purposes very gracefully.
